short_description: Strictly anaerobic, S-layer-coated Gram-positive gut bacillus that grows as a long slender rod with peritrichous flagella and forms a swelling subterminal endospore, giving the classic club silhouette; when antibiotics thin the gut microbiota it overgrows the colon and its toxins TcdA and TcdB cause antibiotic-associated diarrhoea and pseudomembranous colitis.
do_not_draw: A Gram-negative double envelope: no outer membrane, no membrane-periplasm-membrane sandwich, no LPS / O-antigen fringe. This organism is Gram-positive (plasma membrane, thick peptidoglycan wall, S-layer).
A coccus, sphere, diplococcus or grape-cluster arrangement — it is a long slender rod.
A thick polysaccharide capsule dominating the outline; the S-layer is a thin paracrystalline protein sheath, and a true capsule in this species is contested.
An endospore drawn dead-centre in the cell, or capping the very tip — it is SUBTERMINAL, with a clear length of ordinary slim rod continuing beyond it to the pole.
A spore free-floating outside or beside the cell as if it were a separate organism.
A virus-like geometric or icosahedral capsid, spikes, or any phage-like symmetry.
A mesosome (chemical-fixation artefact, not a real structure).
The nucleoid as a tidy little circular loop or cartoon plasmid ring — it is an irregular, lobed, condensed DNA mass.
Membrane-bound organelles: no nucleus, mitochondria, ER or Golgi.
Polar flagellar tufts only — the flagella are peritrichous, distributed over the whole body.
An open-air / soil-with-blue-sky setting; the clinical context is the oxygen-free gut lumen next to colonic epithelium.
Saturated 'true colour' implying a real pigment — this species has none.
colour_note: No pigment. Vegetative cells are colourless/translucent; colonies are flat, irregular, grey to off-white and non-haemolytic (the barnyard p-cresol odour and the chartreuse fluorescence at ~360-365 nm are metabolite effects, not visible pigment). Every colour in a published SEM/TEM of this species is digital false colour. Colour in these renders is therefore a didactic legend, kept identical across all four styles: slate-blue S-layer, sage-green peptidoglycan wall, violet plasma membrane, warm ivory-amber cytoplasm, dusty blue-purple nucleoid, teal ribosomes, pale-gold spore core, pale-sage spore cortex, dark umber laminated spore coat, coral-pink flagella.

reference.note: High native resolution, nothing upscaled. Greyscale with an instrument data band and a 10 um scale bar baked in; cleaned with edit_image.py (real-02) to isolate individual rods, strip the data band and apply a natural false colour.

morphology_notes: Straight to slightly curved Gram-positive bacillus, 0.5-1.9 um wide x 3.0-16.9 um long (Bergey's/ABIS; clinical sources quote the everyday 3-6 x ~0.5 um) — for illustration, roughly five to fifteen times longer than wide. Pleomorphic; singly, in pairs or short chains. Envelope inside-out: plasma membrane, thick peptidoglycan wall carrying PS-I/PS-II cell-wall polysaccharides, paracrystalline S-layer from the Cwp84-cleaved SlpA precursor (HMW inner + LMW outer subunits, ~15% of cell mass). NO outer membrane, NO LPS. Caveat: cultures older than ~48 h decolourise and stain Gram-variable/negative — a staining artefact of an ageing thick wall, not a real double envelope. Motility is strain-variable; motile strains carry peritrichous flagella (glycosylated FliC, pro-inflammatory via TLR5). A capsule was reported by ruthenium-red EM in 1989 but is labile and contested — do not draw a dominant capsule. Sporulation gives a single oval SUBTERMINAL endospore that visibly swells and distends the rod, producing the diagnostic club / tennis-racquet silhouette. SOURCE DISAGREEMENT FLAGGED: a minority of references describe the spore as terminal in some strains; the majority and standard teaching description is subterminal. Spore layers inside-out: core (dehydrated cytoplasm with chromosome + Ca-dipicolinate) with inner forespore membrane and germ cell wall, modified-peptidoglycan cortex, laminated proteinaceous inner + outer coat, outermost bumpy exosporium with hair-like BclA projections sitting directly on the coat with no interspace gap (two exosporium morphotypes from one clonal culture). Obligate anaerobe, extremely oxygen-sensitive as a vegetative cell; niche is the anaerobic colonic lumen and the mucus layer over the epithelium after antibiotics disrupt the resident microbiota. Only the spore survives oxygen, persisting for months on surfaces and resisting alcohol — hence soap-and-water handwashing and chlorine-based sporicidal cleaning. Germination is triggered by taurocholate-family primary bile acids plus glycine and inhibited by secondary bile acids from an intact microbiota (7alpha-dehydroxylation by Clostridium scindens and relatives).
